situation (example wording): "compare the national murder trend with baltimore both indexed to 100 in 2018", "Plot the homicide rate in Baltimore and the homicide rate nationally indexed to the earliest date you have", "chart rolling 12 month homicides indexed to 2018 in new york city, baltimore, philadelphia, and washington DC"
what the app does today: No rule: an indexed series was asked about or declined.
proposed behavior: A series "indexed to 100 in <year>" (or "indexed to <year>", "indexed to the earliest date") is computed for each place as its value in each period divided by its own value in the base period, times 100, one decimal, the places side by side. The base is the year named ("the earliest date": the first period in which every place has a figure, one base for all the places, and the answer says which). A rolling 12-month series is indexed to the rolling total of the base year's December (the calendar base year). The table keeps the raw figures beside the index, and one line says how: "Each place's figure divided by its own <base> figure, times 100." A place whose base figure is blank or zero has no index, and the line says so. The figures follow the source and rules the plain series would (P01, P14, P154 for rolling totals).
exact default or choices offered: Index = value / base value x 100 per place, side by side; raw figures in the table; the one line.
